content.comment_body: Thanks for helping me with the analog output dimming using a push button. Now I have another question: I want to use the same analog output and control it with a push button through the web interface on my mobile device. I purchased a new [product_name] with [version_no] and in the [product_name], there is a push button, but pressing it continuously doesn’t change anything—a signal is only sent when I release the button. It behaves like a rising and falling edge signal, not a continuous one.

Hello [user_name], please avoid posting unrelated questions in existing discussions so moderators don’t have to move your post to a separate topic. Using a push button on the enhanced web interface can lead to problems because network delays can affect responsiveness.
Okay, I’ll create a new post for future questions. Sorry for the inconvenience.

Try adjusting the timing setting. I had to increase the delay to 1.0s, as 0.5s was too short for push button control over ethernet. Also, next time please mention which [product_name] and [version_no] you’re using.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is working to control an analog output dimmer with a push button via the web interface using [product_name] and [product_name] on a mobile device. They note the web-based push button only triggers on release, preventing continuous dimming when the button is held down. Issues with timing and network delays are noted, impacting intuitive control and responsiveness through the web interface.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the software push button in [product_name] to function like a physical button, registering and responding to continuous input while pressed, allowing for real-time analog output dimming.
